ask.text: How should the button show that it is ON, so nobody has to guess? For example, a Bold button in an editor looks pressed in; you could also add a small tick or dot.
ask.why: It decides what the button looks like in each state and what the tests check: a pressed look alone keeps the button unchanged in size; a tick or dot adds a visible mark that still works when colours are hard to tell apart.

options.label: Pressed look plus a small check mark when on
options.consequence: On reads clearly even for people who cannot tell the colours apart; the check animates in and out and is hidden from screen readers, which hear 'pressed' instead.

options.label: Pressed look only (filled/tinted background, inset)
options.consequence: Cleanest and smallest; relies on colour and shading alone to tell on from off.

options.label: Pressed look plus the developer chooses the on and off icons
options.consequence: Most flexible (for example a sun and a moon), but the developer must supply icons or on looks like off.

coverage.note: Developers installing the library; decided: a toggle mode on ZestButton.
On/off value is held either by the app or by the button; will be assumed unless it changes what the builder sees.
A UI library with no records, sign-in or ownership.
Toggle mode combined with confirm or dropdown behaviour will be defined as a default.
How on, off, disabled and busy look; asking how ON is communicated.
Rapid repeated clicks flip once per click and are ignored while busy, as the existing busy options do.
A single control; no lists, paging or searching.
No personal data is collected or kept.
Light/dark/system themes, keyboard, aria-pressed, rem sizing, React 18 and 19, additive change.

assumptions: Toggle mode is additive: it is off unless the developer turns it on, so existing buttons look and behave exactly as before.
Rapid repeated clicks flip the state once per click and are ignored while the button is busy.
Toggle mode together with confirmation or a dropdown is defined by default rather than asked about.
